searches.reason: Explore a structural alternative to recent-cutoff sampling: jointly learned time-gap and relative-position attention inside one BERT4Rec. Seek efficient approaches that distinguish persistent affinity from short-lived context using observed timestamps, without assuming that recent purchases imply unresolved demand. Preserve strict-prefix terminal supervision and appended-MASK inference; test temporal attention separately from sampling changes.

searches.reason: Investigate whether context-specific discrimination can improve through an auxiliary contrastive objective within the same BERT4Rec, rather than further changing cutoff probabilities. The weaker sampled training margins in Electronics and Industrial_and_Scientific motivate this direction but do not establish its benefit. Look for false-negative-aware methods that preserve repeated interactions and need neither independently fitted teachers nor inference score fusion.

searches.reason: Explore learning finer item distinctions from supplied titles and descriptions through a small text encoder trained jointly from scratch with BERT4Rec. This could help separate broadly related products from specific functional or stylistic matches, although text cannot establish current need. Prioritize lightweight shared-network designs requiring no external data, pretrained weights, or separately fitted semantic scores.
